version.changelog: Accuracy pass on permissions and troubleshooting. Corrects the scope description to the real full-mailbox OAuth grant (was 'scoped to the mailbox'), documents that gmail_fetch_emails defaults max_results to 1, adds the Gmail query-operator list, the spam/trash exclusion, and label-ids-vs-names. Rewrites the 403 row to lead with placeholder/example IDs (the most common real cause) instead of scopes, and adds a row for tokens invalidated by a Google password change.

llm.summary: This Gmail skill is openly documented, but it asks users to trust a third-party hosted service and plugin with full Gmail mailbox access.

dimensions.detail: Full Gmail mailbox access through a hosted intermediary is purpose-aligned for the complete feature set but broader than users may need for read-only or limited tasks.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The install instructions add an unpinned third-party ClawLink plugin to OpenClaw's allowed tools and restart the gateway; the artifact does not include plugin source, digest, provenance, or local enforcement details.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses the ClawLink flow, full Gmail OAuth scope, and requires user confirmation before writes, including sends and destructive actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact says nothing runs on a timer and nothing durable lives locally, but the OpenClaw allowlist change persists and ClawLink stores OAuth tokens server-side until revoked or disconnected.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The Gmail read, search, draft, send, label, archive, trash, and delete capabilities match the stated inbox-copilot purpose, but they are high-impact because they cover sensitive mailbox contents and write actions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable granting ClawLink and its plugin full access to your Gmail account, including reading mail, sending mail, modifying labels, and deleting messages. Prefer a separate or lower-risk Google account if testing, review Google's consent screen carefully, and revoke access from Google account permissions when you no longer need it.
llm.findings: [T08] expected: The reported full Gmail access and ClawLink dependency are disclosed and coherent with the advertised Gmail features, but the unpinned external plugin and hosted token custody create a material Review concern rather than evidence of malicious behavior.
